# The Great Wood · Book II, pp. 200–209
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	200
P	Stonetop sits on a bluff overlooking the Great Wood, which stretches hundreds of miles to the east. Few villagers dare to even cross the <b>Stream</b> (page 396) that flows near the base of the bluff. Hunters, trappers, and foragers go deeper, but even they venture a day or two into the forest at most.
H2	Impressions
HR
H3	Always
B	Massive trunks, reaching up up up, some bigger around than houses
B	Pale sky glimpsed through the canopy
B	Trees bending, creaking, rustling in the wind
B	A skittering in the distance
B	A sense of smallness, of being swallowed up by something ancient and vast
HR
ICON	icons/spring.svg
H3	Spring
B	Feet slipping on mud, rotting leaves
B	Drip drip dripping of snowmelt, rain, mist
B	Pale buds and early blooms, blue and yellow and violet
B	Hopeful swell of birdsong
P	The terrain is hilly and rugged, laced with small streams and dotted with ponds. The trees are a mix of deciduous and evergreen.
P	In some spots, the trees grow tightly, surrounded by thick brush so that one can barely walk. In others, massive old growth trees dominate, the space between them sparse and open.

PAGE	201
H2	The Compact
HR
P	For generations, the people of Stonetop have kept their promise to the <b>Forest Folk</b> (page 150): they never cut down a living tree in the Great Wood. The villagers gather deadfall, but timber comes from elsewhere.
Q	According to the elders, when did someone last break the compact? What happened to them?
Q	Who's been pushing to start harvesting trees, since the Forest Folk seem to have vanished?
P	What will happen if someone fells a living tree? That's for you to decide. Maybe…
E	they suffer the <b>Forest's Wrath</b> (page 315);
E	they risk releasing an evil spirit, held captive by the tree's roots;
E	the trees house the spirits of dead Forest Folk, and they've just created a <b>specter</b> (page 79); or
E	nothing—unless the Forest Folk return.
H2	Questions
HR
Q	Who in your family used to ply the Wood? How did they lose their nerve?
Q	What did you see deep in the Wood that you've never told to another?
Q	Who did you lose to the Wood? How?
Q	Of all the stories you've heard of the Wood, which one scares you most?

HR
B	A villager wanders off into the Wood for unknown reasons
B	A hunter stumbles home, having narrowly escaped some new danger
B	A southern scholar arrives in Stonetop, seeking a guide into the Great Wood
B	A hunter or trapper who the PCs care about hasn't returned home
B	Trappers are catching strange game: sickly, mutated, and wrong
PAGE	202
TH	steading improvement
C	<b>GREAT WOOD TIMBER</b>
P	Requires all of the following:
C	Proof that trees can be felled without dire consequence
C	A crew of brave lumberjacks
C	A skilled carpenter, working full time
C	Pulling Together once, over a course of a few weeks, to generate the first load of timber.
P	When you <b><i>mark all the requirements</i></b>, increase Fortunes by 1 and add "Timber from the Great Wood" to the Resources list.
P	Henceforth, the steading has a ready supply of timber for improvements and other projects, and it consumes 1 less Surplus every winter.

HR

P	deer, fowl, rabbits, etc.

HR

P	2 A place <b>haunted</b> by death and the undying (page 68)

P	6 A ruin or artifact of the <b>Green Lords</b> (page 210) If it's been there for at least 10 years, it's likely marked by Forest Folk <b>glyphs</b> (page 152).

H3	Butcherbird
P	<i>Horde</i>, <i>tiny</i>, <i>organized</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 1; <b>Armor</b> 1 (<i>tiny</i>)
P	<b>Damage</b> peck d6-2 (<i>hand</i>, <i>messy</i>, 2 piercing)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to feast on bloody, bloody meat
P	• Grab on and stab stab stab
P	• Fend off any who would steal the flock's meal
P	• Scent blood from miles away
P	About the size of a woodpecker, with black and wine-red plumage, flitting about in small flocks (2d6+4). Their laugh will make your blood run cold. But don't worry. They'll get your blood flowing again, real soon.
P	<b>Something interesting:</b> Butcherbirds can smell fresh blood from miles away, and might descend on a hunter's kill to gorge.
P	<b>Something useful:</b> They can smell the blood of their own, and shun it; smeared butcherbird blood is an excellent repellent.

H3	Cave bear
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>large</i>, <i>cautious</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 16; <b>Armor</b> 1 (fur, hide)
P	<b>Damage</b> claws, bite, hug d10+4 (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>, <i>forceful</i>, <i>messy</i>, 1 piercing)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to fill its belly, to protect its young
P	• Rend, maul, crush
P	• Move with surprising speed and grace
P	• Sniff out food, or trouble
P	Great big silver-brown things, eating anything they can dig up or catch. They mostly hibernate through winter, and get especially bold and ornery in autumn as they try to fatten up. They've been known to wake up and forage even in winter, though.
P	They lair in big caves, usually two mates and maybe their cubs. Out and about, the bulls are usually found on their own; the sows on their own, or with their cubs.
P	They're not usually aggressive towards people—unless surprised, extra hungry, or protecting the cubs. Then? Watch out.
ICON	icons/beast.svg
H3	Ceirwmawr
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>large</i>, <i>terrifying</i>, <i>fearless</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 16; <b>Armor</b> 0 <b>Damage</b> hoof d10+1 (<i>close</i>) or antlers d10+3 (<i>reach</i>, <i>forceful</i>)
P	<b>Special quality</b> awe-inspiring antlers <b>Instinct</b> to tolerate no disrespect
P	• Toss aside a barrier or foe
P	• Suffer harm without flinching
P	• Make a show of strength
P	Majestic. Proud. Antlers so large you can scarce believe how deftly it moves through the woods. They are the royalty of deer. It is said that only the Pale Hunter can give them chase, and that any mortal who dares to stalk them quickly finds the tables turned.
H3	Questions
Q	What special property does folklore say the ceirwmawr's antlers possess?
Q	What dire fate is said to befall those who slay a ceirwmawr without the Pale Hunter's permission?

P	• Bite down and rake (<i>messy</i>)
P	They don't usually hunt people. But when game is scarce, or some fool provokes them, they sometimes get a taste for human blood. Even then, they mostly leave groups alone, waiting for someone to fall behind or wander off. Mostly.

H3	Cwisarff
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>small</i>, <i>stealthy</i>, <i>cautious</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 10; <b>Armor</b> 0 <b>Damage</b> venomous bite d10 (<i>close</i>)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to defend its current spot
P	• Wait patiently to spring on prey
P	• Hiss menacingly at a threat
P	• Bite quickly and ready to strike again
P	The vaunted "tree adder," most lethal serpent in the Wood, up to 6 feet long and dripping with venom. In warm months, they hunt and bask in the canopy or sunny clearings. In colder months, they hide in hollows and under logs, going into torpor in winter. They don't hunt people, but they don't fear them either.
P	When you are bitten by a cwisarff, mark a debility in addition to taking damage.
P	Until the poison is treated, you can't regain HP and are in danger of further damage and debility.
ICON	icons/beast.svg
H3	Cynddaraig
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>large</i>, <i>terrifying</i>, <i>fearless</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 20; <b>Armor</b> 2 (scales)
P	<b>Damage</b> three-inch long teeth d10+3 (<i>close</i>, <i>reach</i>, <i>grabby</i>, <i>messy</i>, 3 piercing, advantage)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to dominate its territory
P	• Roar and unfurl its quills, making even brave warriors quail
P	• Bite a limb clean off
P	• To lose itself in primal fury
P	The mighty "rage drake," almost 10 feet tall and 20 feet from nose to tip of tail. Its jaws are full of knives. Blood-red patterns surround its eyes. A frill of feathered quills sprouts from its neck and runs down its back. Maybe a half-dozen of them stalk the whole Great Wood, and one hasn't been spotted near Stonetop for generations (Tor be praised).
P	<b>Something interesting:</b> They prey mostly on large game (wisents, tal gerdwyr, etc.).
P	They'll attack people, but rarely hunt them.
P	<b>Something useful:</b> They attack people to establish dominance, seeing us as rivals. An appropriate offering or show of obeisance might calm one enough for you to get the hell out of there.

H3	Feathered drake
P	<i>Group</i>, <i>stealthy</i>, <i>organized</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 6; <b>Armor</b> 1 (feathers, scales)
P	<b>Damage</b> boney crest d8+2 (<i>close</i>, <i>forceful</i>), talon & teeth d8+2 (<i>hand</i>, <i>messy</i>, 1 piercing)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> flightless
P	<b>Instinct</b> to spring on unwary prey
P	• Burst out of the brush
P	• Bash prey to the ground, senseless
P	• Surround downed prey, and rend
P	Bigger than a grown man, with a talon yea-long on each foot and that ridge on their heads they use to go crashing through the undergrowth. They might follow a party for days, waiting for them to let their guard down or for someone to fall behind.
P	Then? Bam.
P	Their feathers are much-sought by merchants. You can harvest a bundle ◇ of drake feathers (<i>fragile</i>, Value 3) from a flock of 3-4 drakes.
ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Gylglyd vines
P	<b>Damage</b> strangling vines d6 (<i>hand</i>, <i>grabby</i>)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to lure prey
P	• Ensnare their senses with beauty
P	• Lull their minds with euphoric scents
P	• Slowly entwine them, unnoticed, and hold them fast
P	Thick, velvety green vines that drape entire groves or clearings, speckled with flowers of iridescent blue and pink and yellow. The mind reels to see them, wanting to move closer. The flowers give off the sweetest scent, erasing all cares. But the wary might notice strange bulges in the hanging vines, or white bone beneath the carpet.
P	<b>Something interesting</b>: Gylglyd flowers are prized by herbalists and apothecaries, but nearly impossible to cultivate.
P	<b>Something useful</b>: A kerchief soaked in musk can counter the euphoric effect.

H3	Hagr
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>large</i>, <i>terrifying</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 16; <b>Armor</b> 1 (blubbery hide)
P	<b>Damage</b> meaty hands d10+3 (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>, <i>grabby</i>, <i>forceful</i>) or tree trunk d10+5 (<i>reach</i>, <i>area</i>, <i>crude</i>, <i>forceful</i>) or hurled heavy thing d10+3 (<i>thrown</i>, <i>forceful</i>)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to compulsively shape its environment
P	• Fix someone with its evil eye, overwhelming them with fear
P	• Pluck things from the ground as if weightless
P	• Obsessively stack things to exacting standards
P	• Throw a tantrum when things aren't just right
P	Misshapen brutes with sagging flesh and one bulging eye so filled with hate it'll stop you dead in your tracks. They spend their days collecting fallen branches, looking for just the right one to add to their home of rotting logs. The others they pile neatly, reverently. Perhaps they were servants of the Green Lords, once bred to build, and now, long ages hence, building still.

H3	Nailadd
P	<i>Group</i>, <i>cunning</i>, <i>stealthy</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 6; <b>Armor</b> 2 (carapace)
P	<b>Damage</b> venomous bite d8 (<i>hand</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> webs, prodigious leaps <b>Instinct</b> to capture prey and slowly consume it
P	• Leap on prey and knock it prone
P	• Inject a paralytic venom
P	• Drag helpless prey into the canopy and cocoon it
P	So far, these hound-sized spiders have thankfully avoided hunters and trappers in the Wood. They certainly haven't come near town. But they're out there, rest assured, and growing in numbers.
P	<b>Something interesting:</b> Nailadd venom paralyzes prey, rather than killing it.
P	<b>Something useful:</b> You can harvest the venom (d4 uses, <i>dangerous</i>, <i>reload</i>, Value 1) from an intact corpse. When you <b><i>coat a</i></b> <b><i>blade in nailadd venom</i></b>, it deals +1d4 extra damage and numbs the wounded area.

H3	Raselbaedd
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>large</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 20; <b>Armor</b> 4 (hide, unnatural resilience)
P	<b>Damage</b> gore d10+5 (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>, <i>forceful</i>, <i>messy</i>, 3 piercing)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> iron hide, always hungry, easily provoked, afraid of fire
P	<b>Instinct</b> to hold a grudge
P	• Rip things apart: armor, weapons, flesh
P	• Eat almost anything
P	• Refuse to back off or let go, even when dying
P	• Recover from even mortal wounds, over time
P	When a boar lives long enough, and survives enough close calls, and dines year after year on the roots and nuts of ferro trees, it eventually becomes a raselbaedd.
P	The size of a horse, with tusks like short spears and a hide that's crisscrossed with scars and that bristles with broken blades.
P	When you <b><i>deal 2 damage or less to a raselbaedd</i></b>, <b><i>before armor,</i></b> your weapon chips or shatters on its hide.
P	A raselbaedd's hide (<i>immobile</i>, Value 2) can be harvested by a competent hunter with a fine steel blade (2 piercing, Value 2). It can then be fashioned into 1d4 raselbaedd ◇ cuirasses (2 armor, Value 3). Doing so
P	requires:
C	An exceptional tanner
C	An upgraded workshop with fine steel tools (Value 3)
C	A season of labor per cuirass

P	The Forest Folk would sometimes tell stories of the "tall walkers," drakes with necks like trees and bodies like small hills, draped in feathers that look like vines and leaves.
P	Supposedly, they roam deep in the forest, blithely chewing leaves from the canopy and singing mournful songs to each other.
